text:
sheridan: Heads-up — saw a 3x tail latency spike in shared-pool eu-west-1 between 08:12–08:20. GPU util ~98% and queue depth for short requests blew up. suspect noisy tenant `marketeer-prod`.

jordan: saw it too, linked panel: https://grafana.redwood/eu-west/shared-pool :eyes: queue latency graph spikes around 08:14.

maria: is admission control firing? backlog looks dominated by tiny requests (<=64 tokens) that are preventing long-running streams from starting.

ops-bot: AUTO-ALERT: SHARED_POOL_EUW_HIGH_LOAD (2062001234) — threshold breached. auto-scaling not effective due to capacity limits.

jordan: hypothesis: bursty low-token workloads are gaming the scheduler fairness. They create lots of small slots and keep preemption credit low.

sheridan: we discussed hard fencing before, but that broke latency for paying premium tenants. thinking about a middle path: soft-throttle + per-tenant burst smoothing so a tenant can't sustain >X qps for Ys without cooling.

maria: +1. also we could convert accounting to token-credits instead of request-counts so tiny requests pay for scheduling overhead.

jordan: sketch of config i want to try in canary:

```yaml
admission:
  mode: soft-throttle
  accounting: token_credits
  per_tenant:
    burst_window: 30s
    max_burst_tokens: 2000
    smoothing_alpha: 0.6
    min_guarantee_tokens: 500
  preemption:
    window: 60s
    prefer_fallback: true
```

maria: looks reasonable. token_credits maps better to our cost model (gpu-time ~= tokens). keeps tiny requests honest.

sheridan: operational concerns: 1) need robust metrics for "tenant_score" and "burst_age" so we can alert when smoothing thrashes; 2) ensure KV cache warmers don't get evicted immediately (we should add a short pin for warm cache entries).

jordan: agree on metrics. for canary i’ll add tenant_score, token_consumption_1m, burst_count_30s and expose them in per-tenant dashboard.

maria: i can build a quick replay harness to simulate mixed tenants (many small QPS vs few streaming requests) to validate tail latency and throughput.

sheridan: what about premium tenants? we could offer guaranteed min_guarantee_tokens for paid tiers, but we need to be careful with pinned cache — that can starve others. Prefer soft priority (weight multiplier) instead of hard pin.

jordan: noted. we'll implement min_guarantee_tokens as a weight multiplier in the admission allocator rather than hard pins.

ops-bot: NOTE: deploy-bot queued canary to eu-west-1 on tuesday 02:00 UTC when infra window opens.

sheridan: plan: jordan will land scheduler change behind flag + canary in eu-west, maria runs replay tests and sanity checks, i’ll own dashboards/alerts. target: roll canary Mon/Tue and evaluate 48h.

jordan: will do — ramping plan: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% over 3 windows, monitor tenant_score and tail-p50/p95/p99.

maria: will add regression tests for throughput and a script to inject synthetic noisy tenants.

sheridan: follow-ups: create a short runbook for "noisy-tenant incident" and add an ops playbook entry. I'll file the runbook in #eng-platform-runbooks. :thumbsup:

jordan: filed a PR draft for config and allocator changes, link when ready.

maria: ping me for replay infra creds.

sheridan: thanks — keeping this thread for runbook notes and canary updates.
